agreed_facts: For the three months ended May 31, 2026, reported revenue was $8.222 million versus $5.140 million, EBITDA was $4.685 million versus $3.628 million, net income was $2.948 million versus $2.256 million, and diluted EPS was $0.12 versus $0.09, all year-over-year increases.

Water and wastewater revenue rose to $4.659 million from $2.129 million, and water deliveries rose to 631 acre-feet from 76 acre-feet; the company attributed or linked continued demand partly to oil-and-gas activity through the remainder of 2026.
Lot sales revenue increased to $3.006 million from $2.526 million, while water taps sold increased to 66 from 40 and wastewater taps sold increased to 48 from 40.

Management expects Phase 2D to be substantially complete by fiscal year-end, approximately 159 Phase 2E lots in fiscal 2027, and approximately $14.8 million of milestone and finished-lot payments over the next 12 months.
Single-family rental revenue increased to $231 thousand from $131 thousand, and most of 23 contracted units are expected to come online in calendar 2026.
The reported quarter did not produce a change to the earnings model, and the supplied materials do not provide a cash update or two consecutive quarters of permit and tap data.

open_disagreements.topic: Durability of water and wastewater growth
open_disagreements.bull: The 119% revenue increase and eightfold-plus increase in water deliveries demonstrate strong operating momentum, with management expecting oil-and-gas demand to continue through the remainder of 2026.
open_disagreements.bear: The growth may be temporary because the stated demand outlook only extends through the remainder of 2026 and does not establish durable post-2026 demand.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next two quarterly 10-Q filings and the fiscal 2026 10-K should disclose water deliveries, water-and-wastewater revenue by customer or end market, oil-and-gas volumes, contract duration, and management's post-2026 outlook; sustained volumes and revenue after 2026 would support durability, while a sharp reversal would support the temporary-demand concern.

open_disagreements.topic: Sky Ranch execution, payment realization, and builder absorption
open_disagreements.bull: The 19% increase in lot sales, Phase 2D year-end target, expected 159 Phase 2E lots, and $14.8 million payment outlook provide visible monetization catalysts.
open_disagreements.bear: The payment outlook and Phase 2E output remain contingent on construction execution, milestone achievement, and builder absorption, so they are not yet realized revenue or cash.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next 10-Q and fiscal 2026 10-K should report actual Phase 2D completion, lots delivered, signed builder contracts, builder takedowns, milestone receipts, finished-lot payments, accounts receivable, and remaining performance obligations; Arapahoe County or project-level public development and permit records could corroborate physical completion.

open_disagreements.topic: Whether rentals are becoming a meaningful recurring-revenue contributor
open_disagreements.bull: The rental platform is beginning to scale because most of 23 contracted units are expected online in calendar 2026.
open_disagreements.bear: At $231 thousand of quarterly revenue, rentals remain immaterial to current earnings and are not yet evidence of a meaningful recurring-revenue base.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next two 10-Q filings should disclose units placed in service, occupancy, rental revenue, operating costs, and segment profitability; a sustained increase in occupied units and rental revenue over those filings would establish materiality.

open_disagreements.topic: Significance of unchanged forward estimates and absent cash improvement
open_disagreements.bull: The unchanged model reflects reported earnings without deterioration in the operating fundamentals, so the quarter supports rather than weakens the thesis.
open_disagreements.bear: Reported growth did not improve the forward model, and without cash-flow evidence it is unclear whether earnings growth translates into stronger liquidity or durable estimates.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The company's next 10-Q cash-flow statement, balance sheet, debt and liquidity disclosures, together with the next earnings release's updated guidance and consensus estimate revisions, would show whether operating cash flow, collections, capex, and forward assumptions improved.

open_disagreements.topic: Whether peer results support broad utility-sector momentum
open_disagreements.bull: PCYO's broad operating growth, particularly in water, exceeds the available peer revenue trends and supports a constructive sector read-through.
open_disagreements.bear: Peer read-across is mixed despite GWRS strength, so PCYO's results may be company-specific rather than evidence of broad utility momentum.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next publicly filed quarterly reports or earnings releases from PCYO's relevant water peers, including GWRS, should be compared using the same period and definitions for revenue, delivered volumes, customer demand, margins, and guidance; consistent improvement across peers would support broad momentum, while divergent results would support a company-specific explanation.

data.summary: Both sides agree that PCYO reported strong year-over-year growth, with especially large increases in water activity, while Sky Ranch and rental catalysts remain forward-looking management expectations. The unresolved issues are durability of oil-and-gas demand, realization of projected lot payments and absorption, rental materiality, cash conversion and estimate revisions, and the relevance of mixed peer results.
